title: Relational Database Connections

richText: Database connections
A relational database stores data in tables. SQL reads and changes that data.
JDBC is the Java API used to communicate with relational databases. Each database supplies a JDBC driver.
A DataSource supplies database connections to application code. Spring Boot can configure it from dependencies and connection properties.
A connection pool reuses connections instead of opening a new connection for every operation. Spring Boot starters normally use HikariCP when it is available.
Connection setup does not define table mappings or repository methods. Those are separate topics.
Connect to PostgreSQL
Add the PostgreSQL JDBC driver and a database-access starter. Use spring-boot-starter-data-jpa for the JPA lessons.
Configure the database URL, username and password. Keep credentials outside committed source files.
The database must be running and the configured user must have access to it. Spring Boot does not create a PostgreSQL server.

example.title: Configure a PostgreSQL connection
description: Use a Spring Boot 3 project with Java 17 or later.
Add org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-data-jpa and org.postgresql:postgresql to pom.xml. Set the driver dependency scope to runtime.
Create a PostgreSQL database named notes. Set DB_USERNAME and DB_PASSWORD in the application environment.
explanation: The JDBC URL selects the PostgreSQL server and notes database.
validate checks mapped tables when JPA starts. It does not create them.
With no entities yet, this configuration teaches the connection settings. Once entities are added, create their tables before starting with validate.

richText: Create and change the schema
A schema describes database objects such as tables and columns.
For a disposable learning database, ddl-auto=create or create-drop can generate tables from entity mappings. These settings can destroy existing data.
For a persistent database, use versioned migrations such as Flyway or Liquibase to change the schema. Use ddl-auto=validate to check mappings.
ddl-auto=update is not a substitute for reviewed, versioned migrations.
Use H2 for a separate local case
H2 can run inside the application process. An in-memory H2 database keeps its data in memory.
An in-memory database loses its data when it closes. It is useful for short local experiments.
H2 and PostgreSQL can behave differently. Use PostgreSQL when checking PostgreSQL-specific SQL or behavior.

example.title: Configure an in-memory H2 database
description: For this local case, add com.h2database:h2 with runtime scope instead of the PostgreSQL driver.
Use a separate local profile or project. Put these properties in its application.properties.
explanation: jdbc:h2:mem:notes creates an in-memory database named notes.
create-drop creates mapped tables and drops them when the JPA application shuts down normally.
The empty password is for this isolated local example.
